# Vivekakathā (Ps 3.4)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vivekakathā* ("Discussion of Seclusion") is the fourth chapter of the third division (*vagga*) of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*. It preserves what is likely the earliest surviving exegesis of the canonical *viveka-nissita* ("dependent on seclusion") formula [Gethin 2001]. In this exposition, the text delineates five forms of seclusion (*viveka*), paired with five kinds of dispassion (*virāga*), cessation (*nirodha*), and relinquishment (*vossagga*) [Gethin 2001]. For instance, it explains that seclusion from the mental hindrances occurs by suppression (*vikkhambhana*) during the attainment of the first *jhāna*, while seclusion from wrong views occurs by substitution of opposites (*tadaṅga*) through concentration endowed with penetrative wisdom [Gethin 2001].

The treatise has direct textual connections with the Saṁyutta Nikāya, notably the *Balasutta* (SN 45.149) and *Bījasutta* (SN 45.150). Automatic text-reuse analysis shows substantial Pali-internal textual overlap: DharmaNexus matches over one thousand segments across 45 texts, with its largest reuse occurring in the *Magga Saṁyutta* (SN 45, specifically matching the sequence of SN 45.149), the *Bojjhaṅga Saṁyutta* (SN 46), the *Indriya Saṁyutta* (SN 48), and other chapters of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* such as the *Ñāṇakathā* (Ps 1.1) and *Ānāpānassatikathā* (Ps 1.3) [DharmaNexus]. Outside the Pali tradition, DharmaNexus aligns passages of the text with Sanskrit treatises including the *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, *Dharmasaṃgraha*, and *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā*, as well as Chinese Āgama parallels (such as the *Dīrghāgama*) and Tibetan translations of sūtra and tantra literature [DharmaNexus].
